name: Creality Falcon A1 Pro 20W
tagline: Enclosed dual-source A1 Pro: diode plus infrared for more materials
tldr: Creality Falcon A1 Pro 20W adds a dual-laser setup in an enclosed chassis for faster engraving and some metal/plastic marking. Middle ground between A1 10W and the open Falcon 2 Pro 40W line.
mainObjective: Everyday engraving plus reliable light cutting on wood, leather, and dark acrylic

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

pros: Two lasers: a 20W blue diode for cutting and a 2W infrared for bare metal and plastics
Cuts 10 mm basswood and 8 mm black acrylic per Creality's spec
More safety sensors (flame detection, tilt stop, airflow monitoring) plus built-in air assist
cons: About twice the price of the entry A1 ($1,099 on Creality's store, October 2026)
Infrared module inclusion depends on the bundle: check before buying
Infrared marks are shallow: not a replacement for a fiber laser
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 20W SKU on Creality Falcon A1 Pro. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other power options via the chips before buying.
proTips: Use air assist for cuts, lower scan speed for photo engraving. Multiple passes at moderate speed beat one aggressive pass. Check the flagship tier’s cut benchmark if you quote production times to customers.

moduleSystem.headline: Diode + infrared in one enclosure
moduleSystem.description: A1 Pro combines a high-power diode with an infrared source for expanded material support inside the enclosed chassis.

editorialDepth.advantages: Creality Falcon A1 Pro 20W is the versatile hobby / side-business SKU: clean engraving and light wood or leather cuts with comparable benchmarks on Maker Atlas.
editorialDepth.limitations: Not a CO₂ replacement for clear acrylic or heavy thick-stock production.

faq.question: How thick can the Falcon A1 Pro cut?
faq.answer: Creality's spec, quoted in CNX Software's review, lists 10 mm basswood and 8 mm black acrylic; thicker stock needs several passes. In our benchmark a 10 × 10 cm square in 3 mm basswood took about 4–7 min.

faq.question: What does the 2W infrared laser add?
faq.answer: Marking on bare stainless steel, other metals and many plastics, which the blue diode cannot do without spray. It is meant for fine marks on tags, tumblers and tools, not deep engraving. Creality's listing says module inclusion depends on the bundle, so check that the infrared head is in the kit you buy.

faq.question: A1 Pro or A1 10W: which one?
faq.answer: The A1 Pro costs about twice as much ($1,099 against $549 on Creality's store, October 2026). It is the right pick if you need metal marking, AI auto-focus on objects of different heights, or 6–10 mm cuts. For engraving gifts on wood and leather, the A1 10W does the job for half the price.

standoutFeatures.title: Diode and infrared in one box
standoutFeatures.body: The 20W diode cuts and engraves wood, leather and dark acrylic; the 2W infrared head marks bare metals and plastics in the same enclosure.

standoutFeatures.title: AI visual auto-focus
standoutFeatures.body: Creality's visual auto-focus sets the focal height for each object, which saves manual measuring when you engrave items of different thicknesses.
